report.about.data.body: time without CGM data is excluded from all values. A data gap is an interval between two readings that is longer than 15 minutes or three reading intervals, whichever is longer, the reading interval being the median of the 10 intervals before the reading (the higher of the two middle values; filled with the intervals after it at the start of the data; the usual interval of the source with fewer than 3). Each reading represents the time until the next reading, so a shorter dropout counts in full (the values in between are not known); before a gap, only its own reading interval. Sensor active is that time as a share of the period; the CGM system's own figure also counts readings not received for this report (for example during delivery or network outages) and applies its own rules to short dropouts. Every percentage and every statistic weights each reading by the time it represents. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.about.durations.body: d, days; h, hours; min, minutes.
report.about.enough.body: the values of a period (time in ranges, mean glucose, SD, CV, GMI, GRI, lowest and highest value, events and comparisons, also those of a week or a day) are shown only when its sensor active is at least 70%, compared before rounding; otherwise the period's sensor active is given and a dash (-) stands in place of its values. The 70% condition is published for 14-day periods (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2); this report applies it to periods of every length. The glucose profiles and the Daily Log show the readings received in any case. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. A dash (-) also marks a value that does not exist for a period, such as GMI for fewer than 14 days.
report.about.forms.body: The summary contains the 14-day section (time in ranges, glucose metrics, the glucose profile and the daily glucose profiles), the longer-term overview (30 days and longer), the weekly trend (90 days and 6 months), Hypoglycemia, Hyperglycemia, the comparison with the previous period (not in the 6-month report), Data Quality and Laboratory A1C. The full report adds Hypoglycemia Events by Period, the daily glucose profiles of the whole period (30 days and longer), Daily Patterns, the Daily Summary, the Daily Log (one row per day, one column per hour) and the Monthly Summary (every calendar month of the period). The two appendices are added to either form only when chosen. Each section opens with a caption line that names its rule and source, shows its data and ends with Notes that explain them with their sources.
report.about.length.body: Among 257 people with type 1 diabetes, 14 days of CGM data estimated the 3-month time in range and mean glucose closely (Riddlesworth et al., 2018). Time below range is less precise: among 329 people with type 1 diabetes with 90 days of CGM data, its error roughly halved from 10 to 30 days of data and continued to decrease to 60 days (Cichosz et al., 2023).
report.about.limit.body: a reading outside the CGM sensor's measurement range (shown in this report as LO or HI) has no value: it is left out of the mean, the standard deviation, the CV, the GMI, the lowest and highest values and the glucose curves, and it is counted as very low or very high in the time in ranges and in the events, where an event's lowest value can be LO. Its number and time are noted under the statistics. No consensus document addresses such readings, and other software treats them differently: the report software of Abbott Diabetes Care shows them at the limit (Abbott Diabetes Care, 2018, p. 7), so the values can differ from a manufacturer's report. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.about.mmol_mol.body: GMI in mmol/mol = 12.71 + 4.70587 × mean glucose in mmol/L (Bergenstal et al., 2018); laboratory A1C entered in percent converted with the master equation of the International Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (IFCC) and the National Glycohemoglobin Standardization Program (NGSP), mmol/mol = {factor} × (% − {offset}) (Hoelzel et al., 2004). The unit is chosen in the settings.
report.about.not_included.body: food intake, insulin, physical activity and device information are not part of the data.
report.about.period.body: full days ending at midnight before the report was created; the days and the night and day periods follow the time zone of the system that created the report. The first section always shows the most recent 14 days, the recommended period (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2013).
report.about.report.body: GlucoCraft is not affiliated with or endorsed by the cited authors or any CGM manufacturer. The values are calculated from the data received from the glucose sources and can differ from the reports of the CGM manufacturer's software.
report.about.rounding.body: every value is calculated from the readings as stored and rounded once, where it is shown: percentages to one decimal (two where one decimal would show a target's value that the value does not meet), glucose in mg/dL to whole numbers and in mmol/L to one decimal, with halves rounded away from zero. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.about.sources.body: Primary source: {primary}. Second source: {second}. The second source fills only gaps in the primary source's readings, each at its own measurement time; a reading measured by both is counted once, from the primary source.
report.about.sources.body_untimed: Primary source: {primary}. Second source: {second}. The second source fills only gaps in the primary source's readings, each at the time it was received (this source sends no measurement time); a reading measured by both is counted once, from the primary source; it is used only after the primary source has delivered no reading for 5 minutes or three reading intervals, whichever is longer.
report.about.sources.share: In this period, {share} of the readings came from the second source.
report.about.title: About This Report
report.alt.events.one: Hypoglycemia events by time of day: {count} level 1 event, {level_2} of them with a level 2 event; lowest value {lowest}.
report.alt.events.other: Hypoglycemia events by time of day: {count} level 1 events, {level_2} of them with a level 2 event; lowest value {lowest}.
report.alt.limits: Readings at the sensor's limit, which have no value: {kinds}.
report.alt.profile: {title}: median from {median_min} to {median_max}; 5th to 95th percentile from {range_min} to {range_max}.
report.alt.tir: Time in ranges: very low {very_low}, low {low}, in range {in_range}, of which tight range {tight}, high {high}, very high {very_high}.
report.alt.weekly.one: {name} by week, {count} week with values: from {min} to {max}.
report.alt.weekly.other: {name} by week, {count} weeks with values: from {min} to {max}.
report.blocks.gmi_both: GMI in percent (in mmol/mol in the summary above).
report.blocks.notes: One row per 14-day period, oldest first, so that each period can be read in the same way as the 14 days on page 1. A shorter first period is marked with its length; it has no GMI and no GRI. A period with less than 70% sensor active shows its sensor active (Data) and no values, as described in About This Report (Enough data). Consensus targets apply to 14-day periods with at least 70% sensor active (Battelino et al., 2019).
report.blocks.title: Consecutive 14-Day Periods
report.change.not_available: Not available: the previous period of the same length ({previous_start} – {previous_end}) has {active} sensor active (data received), less than the 70% that the values of a period need.
report.change.not_available_this: No comparison: this period has {active} sensor active (data received), less than the 70% that the values of a period need.
report.change.notes: Differences are numerical and carry no clinical interpretation; each is the difference of the two values as shown. The two periods are compared only when both have at least 70% sensor active (data received), as described in About This Report (Enough data).
report.change.six_months: Not part of the 6-month report: a previous period of the same length would require about {days} days of readings, and readings are kept for {retention} days (the 6-month report and the 90-day report with its previous period fit within them).
report.change.title: Comparison with the Previous Period
report.context.both: The 2017 international consensus quantifies hypoglycemia both as the percentage of CGM values, or the minutes or hours, below a threshold and "as the number of hypoglycemic events that occur over the given CGM reporting period" (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4, para. 13). This explains why this section shows both the time below range and the number of events for the same period.
report.context.cv: The 2019 international consensus sets the target for glycemic variability at a coefficient of variation (%CV) of 36% or less (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2), a value it takes from Monnier et al. (2017). The ADA Standards of Care list the same goal of 36% or less ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). This explains the target in the CV row.
report.context.event: The 2017 international consensus states that "readings below the threshold for at least 15 min" are considered an event and that the event ends with readings for 15 minutes at 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or higher (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4, para. 14). This explains how the level 1 and level 2 events in the Hypoglycemia section are counted: an event is counted once its readings have been below its limit for 15 minutes, starts at its first reading below the limit, and ends with 15 minutes at 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or higher.
report.context.forms: The 2019 international consensus describes a single-page report as of value and states that more detailed reports, for example detailed daily reports, "should remain available for individualized review" (Battelino et al., 2019, Standardization of CGM Data Presentation section, para. 2). The American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care recommend a minimum of a single-page report, such as the standardized CGM report and a weekly summary, and state that options for daily and weekly reports and raw data should be available ({ada_b}, Recommendation 7.9). This explains why the CGM Report has a summary and a full report with daily profiles, a daily summary and an hourly log, and why the readings can be exported as comma-separated values (CSV).
report.context.lab_ada: The ADA Standards of Care state that the comparability of A1C and mean CGM glucose depends on the number of days of CGM wear, the timing of the A1C test relative to the CGM period, the accuracy of the meter and the CGM system, the lag between interstitial and venous glucose, and factors that affect A1C or red blood cell turnover ({ada_a}, Correlation Between A1C and Blood Glucose Monitoring and Continuous Glucose Monitoring section, para. 2). This explains why a laboratory result and the GMI of the 90 days before it can differ; the 90-day period is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.context.lab_difference: In the data from which GMI was derived, the GMI and the laboratory A1C differed by 0.3 percentage points or more in 51% of 528 participants and by 0.5 percentage points or more in 28% (Bergenstal et al., 2018, Table 3). This explains why the laboratory results in this section can differ from the GMI shown beside them.
report.context.lab_difference_none: In the data from which GMI was derived, the GMI and the laboratory A1C differed by 0.3 percentage points or more in 51% of 528 participants and by 0.5 percentage points or more in 28% (Bergenstal et al., 2018, Table 3). This explains why a laboratory result entered in this section can differ from the GMI shown beside it.
report.context.names: The 2019 international consensus names the glucose ranges of the standardized report "Very High" (level 2), "High" (level 1), "Low" (level 1) and "Very Low" (level 2) (Battelino et al., 2019, Standardization of CGM Data Presentation section, para. 1). This explains the range names Very high, High, Low and Very low.
report.context.night: The 2017 international consensus reports the glucose metrics in three time blocks, sleep, wake and 24 hours, with default times from midnight to 6 in the morning for sleep and from 6 in the morning to midnight for wake (Danne et al., 2017, Section 7). For clinical trials, the 2023 international consensus statement reports nocturnal data for 00:00 to 05:59 and daytime data for 06:00 to 23:59 (Battelino et al., 2023, Panel 2). This explains the Night ({night}) and Day ({day}) columns of the Hypoglycemia table; the report's night is a clock period, not a measure of sleep.
report.context.patterns: The 2017 international consensus states that "retrospective analysis of CGM is dependent on stability of patterns from day to day" (Danne et al., 2017, Section 7, para. 5). This explains why the glucose profile, which combines all days of the period by time of day, is shown together with the daily glucose profiles of the same days.
report.context.profile: The 2023 international consensus statement on CGM metrics for clinical trials describes four features of the graph of the glucose profile: the target glucose range, the median line, the shaded 25th to 75th percentile band and the outer 5th to 95th percentile band (Battelino et al., 2023, p. 49). This explains the lines and shaded bands of the glucose profile in the CGM Report.
report.context.sufficiency: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care list two conditions for valid CGM data: at least 14 days of wear, and the CGM active for 70% of the time over those 14 days ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). The 2019 international consensus gives the same 14 days and 70%, counted as a share of the possible CGM readings (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2). For this reason, the values of a period are shown only with at least 70% sensor active, GMI and GRI only for periods of 14 days or more, and each section notes a period with less. Sensor active is measured as the share of the period represented by the readings received. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.context.sufficiency_custom: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care list two conditions for valid CGM data: at least 14 days of wear, and the CGM active for 70% of the time over those 14 days ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). The 2019 international consensus gives the same 14 days and 70%, counted as a share of the possible CGM readings (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2). For this reason, the values of a period are shown only with at least 70% sensor active, GMI and GRI only for periods of 14 days or more, each section notes a period with less, and the custom appendix compares a custom goal (met / not met) only for periods that meet both conditions. Sensor active is measured as the share of the period represented by the readings received. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.context.tar: The 2019 international consensus sets the targets for time above range at less than 25% above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and less than 5% above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L), which are less than 6 hours and less than 1 hour and 12 minutes per day (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 3). The 25% target covers levels 1 and 2 together and so includes the time above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). The 2019 consensus defines level 1 hyperglycemia as 181–250 mg/dL (10.1–13.9 mmol/L) and level 2 as above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2). This explains the targets in the rows of the time above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L).
report.custom.caption: The statistics calculated with the ranges and goals set by the user: the user's own settings, not published targets.
report.custom.compared_note: Met / not met compares the value with the custom goal arithmetically; it is not an assessment.
report.custom.not_compared_note: Not compared: less than 70% sensor active in the period.
report.custom.note: Time below range and time above range include the very low and very high readings. Consensus ranges: the value of the main report (Battelino et al., 2019).
report.custom.notes: The main report always uses the consensus ranges. Met / not met is shown only for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019). This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.custom.ranges: very low below {very_low}; low below {low}; in range {low}–{high}; tight range {tight_low}–{tight_high}; high above {high}; very high above {very_high} {unit}
report.custom.title: Appendix: Custom Ranges and Goals — {period}
report.daily.caption: One profile per day, midnight to midnight, as 10-minute means; the shaded band is {t70_180} {unit} (Battelino et al., 2019).
report.daily.notes: Each profile is one day, midnight to midnight, as 10-minute means; each row is one calendar week. A data gap (as defined in About This Report, Data) interrupts the line. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. Values above {t180} and below {t70} {unit} are drawn with a thicker line (in color, in the high and the low color; in grayscale, dashed above {t180} and black below {t70}), and the shaded band is {t70_180} {unit} (consensus thresholds; Battelino et al., 2019); all days use one scale. A LO or HI reading (below or above the CGM sensor's measurement range) has no value: it interrupts the line, and marks along the bottom (LO) or top (HI) edge show where such readings lie.
report.daily.notes_period: The profiles are drawn as the daily glucose profiles of the 14 days; their Notes describe the lines and the band.
report.daily.title: Daily Glucose Profiles — {period}
report.days.caption: One row per day: mean glucose, level 1 hypoglycemia events (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4) and sensor active (data received).
report.days.notes: Level 1 events: at least 15 consecutive minutes below {t70} {unit}, each counted on the day it began. Sensor active as a percentage of the day. A dash (-) means that the day has less than 70% sensor active (the Data column), as described in About This Report (Enough data).
report.days.title: Daily Summary — {period}
report.description: The CGM Report shows the standardized metrics and glucose profile recommended for the Ambulatory Glucose Profile (Battelino et al., 2019; Bergenstal et al., 2013).
report.enough.more.days.one: With no gaps, about {count} more day is needed.
report.enough.more.days.other: With no gaps, about {count} more days are needed.
report.enough.more.hours.one: With no gaps, about {count} more hour is needed.
report.enough.more.hours.other: With no gaps, about {count} more hours are needed.
report.enough.note: {period}: not enough data yet. The report shows a period's statistics once the readings received cover at least 70% of it (sensor active). So far they cover {active}.
report.enough.short.one: Not enough data: sensor active (data received) {active} of {count} day; the values of a period are shown from 70%.
report.enough.short.other: Not enough data: sensor active (data received) {active} of {count} days; the values of a period are shown from 70%.
report.error.period: This report period is not available: {days} days. The CGM Report can be created for 14, 30, 90 or 180 days. Check the card's or automation's settings.
report.events.caption: Level 1 and level 2 hypoglycemia events (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4) in each period ending on the report's last day.
report.events.notes: One column for each period of 14, 30 and 90 days and 6 months that lies within the report period, each ending on the report's last day, with its sensor active (data received). The events, their durations and their levels follow the rule described in the Notes of the Hypoglycemia section (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4); each event is counted in the period in which it starts, and an event that reached level 2 contains at least 15 consecutive minutes below {t54} {unit}. Events per day: the number of events divided by the days of the period; the starts are counted in eight blocks of 3 hours of the local clock. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. Night is {night} (Battelino et al., 2023, Panel 2). The counts are shown without targets. A period with less than 70% sensor active shows its sensor active and no counts, as described in About This Report (Enough data).
report.events.title: Hypoglycemia Events by Period
report.header.sources: Consensus ranges and targets (Battelino et al., 2019); tight range (Battelino et al., 2023). {data}
report.header.title: GlucoCraft CGM Report — Continuous Glucose Monitoring
report.highs.caption: Time above {t180} and above {t250} {unit} by night and day; consensus targets for the whole period (Battelino et al., 2019).
report.highs.notes: The night and day periods are those of the Hypoglycemia section.
report.highs.title: Hyperglycemia — {period}
report.key.title: Consensus ranges, {unit} (Battelino et al., 2019)
report.key.title_hatched: Consensus ranges, {unit} (Battelino et al., 2019); hatched above {t180}
report.lab.caption: Each laboratory A1C result beside the GMI (Bergenstal et al., 2018) of the 90 days ending on its date.
report.lab.difference_both: In the Difference column, the first value is in percentage points and the second in mmol/mol. In mmol/mol, the GMI follows the GMI equation (Bergenstal et al., 2018) and a laboratory A1C entered in percent the master equation (Hoelzel et al., 2004), so two values equal in percent can differ by 1 mmol/mol.
report.lab.error.date: The date must be a calendar date written as year-month-day, for example 2026-10-22.
report.lab.error.future: The date must not be later than today.
report.lab.error.no_date: Enter the date of the blood test.
report.lab.error.range: The A1C must be between {low} and {high} {unit}.
report.lab.error.unit: The unit must be percent or mmol/mol.
report.lab.intro: GMI estimates A1C (glycated hemoglobin, a laboratory blood test) from mean CGM glucose.
report.lab.method: Each laboratory result is compared with the GMI of the 90 days ending on its date; GMI is shown only with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019). This method is a GlucoCraft rule. CGM data are kept for {days} days, so a result whose 90 days begin earlier has no CGM comparison. Difference: the laboratory A1C minus the GMI. Sensor active: data received in the 90 days ending on the date of the test.
report.lab.no_comparison: no CGM comparison (data older than {days} days)
report.lab.none: No laboratory A1C result has been entered.
report.lab.title: Laboratory A1C Compared with GMI

report.legend.events: Events, the level 1 hypoglycemia events that began in the period (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4)
report.legend.gmi: GMI, glucose management indicator (Bergenstal et al., 2018)
report.legend.gri: GRI, Glycemia Risk Index, with its zone A to E (Klonoff et al., 2023)
report.legend.tir: TIR, time in range ({t70_180} {unit}; Battelino et al., 2019)
report.legend.titr: TITR, time in tight range ({t70_140} {unit}; Battelino et al., 2023)
report.license.title: License
report.limit_note.one: {count} reading at the sensor's limit ({parts}), left out of the values and counted in the time in ranges, as described under About This Report.
report.limit_note.other: {count} readings at the sensor's limit ({parts}), left out of the values and counted in the time in ranges, as described under About This Report.
report.log.caption: One row per day and one cell per hour, the hour's maximum above and its minimum below; consensus thresholds (Battelino et al., 2019).
report.log.hours_12: Column heads in the 12-hour format: {h0} is {t0}, {h6} is {t6}, {h12} is {t12} and {h18} is {t18}; the other columns are the hours between them.
report.log.notes_color: An hour with a value below {t70} is shaded by its minimum (dark red, below {t54}; red, below {t70}), any other hour by its maximum (orange, above {t250}; yellow, above {t180}; light gray, in range); blank, no data. The numbers are measured values. LO and HI: a reading below (LO) or above (HI) the CGM sensor's measurement range, whose value is not known. It takes the place of the hour's minimum or maximum and shades the hour as very low or very high.
report.log.notes_gray: An hour with a value below {t70} is shaded by its minimum (darkest, below {t54}; dark, below {t70}), any other hour by its maximum (a hatched edge on dark gray, above {t250}; a hatched edge on lighter gray, above {t180}; light, in range); blank, no data. The numbers are measured values. LO and HI: a reading below (LO) or above (HI) the CGM sensor's measurement range, whose value is not known. It takes the place of the hour's minimum or maximum and shades the hour as very low or very high.
report.log.title: Daily Log — {period}
report.lows.caption: Events: 15 minutes below {t70} (level 1) or {t54} {unit} (level 2), ending after 15 minutes at or above {t70} {unit} (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4).
report.lows.chart_title: Hypoglycemia events by time of day
report.lows.event.body: An event is counted once its readings have been below its limit for 15 minutes, and it then starts at its first reading below the limit. Its duration runs to the first reading of the 15 minutes at or above {t70} {unit}, or to the end of the time its last reading represents when a data gap (as defined in About This Report, Data) follows or the readings end; it is counted in the period in which it starts, a level 2 event in that of its level 1 event. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. No consensus rule exists for these details.
report.lows.notes: Time below range by night and day, and the hypoglycemia events that began in the period (level 1: below {t70} {unit}; level 2: below {t54} {unit}). Level 2 events are also counted as level 1 events. Consensus targets for the whole period (Battelino et al., 2019).
report.lows.scatter_caption: Each marker is one level 1 event, at its start time and lowest value; the marker size increases with the duration, up to 120 minutes. The darker markers are events that contain a level 2 event (at least 15 consecutive minutes below {t54} {unit}; Danne et al., 2017, Section 4). The solid line marks {t70} {unit} and the broken line {t54} {unit}. A lowest value below the CGM sensor's measurement range (LO) is drawn at the sensor's lower limit.
report.lows.title: Hypoglycemia — {period}
report.metrics.sources: CV consensus target (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2). GMI formula (Bergenstal et al., 2018); shown from 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (the condition of Battelino et al., 2019). GRI 0–100; zones A to E are the quintiles of the GRI, from the lowest (first to 20th percentile) to the highest (81st to 100th percentile), and hypoglycemia is weighted more heavily than hyperglycemia (Klonoff et al., 2023). GRI is shown for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active, as GMI; its zone is taken from the GRI value: A up to 20, B up to 40, C up to 60, D up to 80, E above 80. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.metrics.title: Glucose Metrics
report.monthly.caption: Mean glucose of each day and the level 1 hypoglycemia events that began that day (Danne et al., 2017, Section 4).
report.monthly.notes: Mean glucose per day ({unit}) at the bottom of each day; at the upper right, where there are any, the number of level 1 hypoglycemia events (at least 15 consecutive minutes below {t70} {unit}) that began that day; the day of the month at the upper left. A dash (-) means that the day has less than 70% sensor active, as described in About This Report (Enough data). The monthly summary covers every calendar month of the report period; a month only partly in the period shows only the days of the period, and its heading names them.
report.monthly.title: Monthly Summary — {period}
report.notes.title: Notes
report.overview.caption: Consensus ranges and targets (Battelino et al., 2019); tight range (Battelino et al., 2023), no clinical-care consensus target.
report.overview.notes: CV target (Battelino et al., 2019; Monnier et al., 2017); GMI (Bergenstal et al., 2018); GRI (Klonoff et al., 2023). The lowest and highest values are single measured readings, as stored; a reading at the sensor's limit (LO or HI) has no value and is left out of them.
report.overview.per_day_note: A time in parentheses beside a percentage is that percentage of 24 hours (1% of time = {minutes} minutes per day).
report.overview.profile_notes: All readings of the whole period combined by time of day, with the same lines, percentile bands, shaded band and edge marks as the 14-day glucose profile.
report.overview.title: Longer-Term Overview — {period}
report.page1.notes.groups.body: The consensus also publishes different targets for some groups, such as older or high-risk adults and pregnancy (Battelino et al., 2019, Tables 3 and 4). They are not included here. The results here are calculated with the ranges and targets for adults in general, not with the ranges for these groups.
report.page1.notes.metrics.body: mean glucose and the standard deviation (SD) are weighted by time, as described in About This Report (Data). Coefficient of variation (CV) = SD ÷ mean glucose × 100 (Danne et al., 2017). Glucose management indicator (GMI) in percent = 3.31 + 0.02392 × mean glucose in mg/dL (Bergenstal et al., 2018). Glycemia Risk Index (GRI) = 3.0 × very low + 2.4 × low + 1.6 × very high + 0.8 × high, each in percent of time, at most 100; its hypoglycemia component is very low + 0.8 × low and its hyperglycemia component very high + 0.5 × high (Klonoff et al., 2023).
report.page1.notes.profile.body: The cited sources do not describe the smoothing of the profile; each 15-minute period is pooled with the two neighboring periods (45 minutes), and each reading counts once for every whole minute it represents. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.page1.notes.ranges.body: international consensus only (Battelino et al., 2019): in range {t70_180} {unit} (more than 70%), below {t70} (less than 4%, including below {t54}), below {t54} (less than 1%), above {t180} (less than 25%, including above {t250}), above {t250} (less than 5%), CV 36% or less (Battelino et al., 2019; Monnier et al., 2017). Tight range {t70_140} {unit} (Battelino et al., 2023); no clinical-care consensus target.

report.profile.lines: All readings of the period combined by time of day: the median (50th percentile), the interquartile range (25th to 75th percentile) and the 5th to 95th percentile range, in 15-minute periods. The shaded band is {t70_180} {unit}, the solid lines mark {t70} and {t180} {unit} and the broken lines {t54} and {t250} {unit}, each where it lies within the chart's scale; in color, the bands and the median take the color of the range they lie in. Marks along the bottom (LO: below the CGM sensor's measurement range) or top (HI: above it) edge show the times of day with such readings, which have no value.

report.quality.caption: The CGM data of the period; valid CGM data: 14 days with at least 70% sensor active (Battelino et al., 2019, Table 2).
report.quality.gap_rule: Data gaps and sensor active are as defined in About This Report, Data. Time without data: the length of the period minus the time the readings represent. Days with CGM data: the days of the period with any time represented by readings. Data gaps: the number of gaps that overlap the period, and the longest of them at its full length, also where it extends beyond the period. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.quality.sensor_change: sensor change at {start}, without a warm-up time
report.quality.sensor_events: Sensor changes and warm-ups detected in the data: {events}.
report.quality.sensor_events_method: A new sensor is detected when the stated sensor expiry (where one is provided) moves more than a day later, or when the source reports the warm-up marker that some CGM systems send; the warm-up ends at the first valid reading, or after 24 hours without one. A change that neither shows is not detected. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
report.quality.strip_note: The strip shows the sensor active of each day; a gray cell is a day without data.

report.research.caption: Extended high-glucose events as defined for clinical trials (Battelino et al., 2023, p. 48), without targets.
report.research.definition: An event is a period in which sensor glucose stays above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) for at least 120 minutes. It ends when glucose has returned to 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) or below for 15 minutes (Battelino et al., 2023, p. 48). This definition was made for counting events in clinical trials: the 2023 international consensus statement lists the "extended hyperglycaemic event rate" as a secondary endpoint for clinical studies (Battelino et al., 2023, p. 48). The same statement also describes extended hyperglycemia as 90 cumulative minutes above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) within a 120-minute period (Battelino et al., 2023, Table 4); this report uses the version that states both a start and an end.
report.research.intro: This appendix shows measures that research publications define but that the clinical-care standards do not. They are not part of the main report, they have no targets, and they are shown without color or comparison.
report.research.limits: Only the readings received for this report are counted. An event during a gap in the data is not counted, or is counted shorter. The CGM system's own data can contain readings that were not received for this report.
report.research.method.1: The readings are the CGM values received for this report, in mg/dL; a HI reading counts at the sensor's upper limit (always above 250 mg/dL). The limits in mmol/L are 13.9 and 10.0.
report.research.method.2: Start: a run of consecutive readings, each above 250 mg/dL, becomes an event once the time it covers reaches 120 minutes. The time a run covers is measured as in all statistics of this report: each reading counts until the next reading, or for its own reading interval before a data gap. The event's start time is the time of the run's first reading.
report.research.method.3: During the event, readings from 181 to 250 mg/dL do not end it.
report.research.method.4: End: the event ends at the first reading of the first run of readings at or below 180 mg/dL that covers 15 minutes. Its duration is the time from its start to that reading.
report.research.method.5: Data gaps: a data gap (an interval between two readings that is longer than 15 minutes or three reading intervals, whichever is longer) ends a running event at the end of its last reading before the gap, which counts for its own reading interval. A run above 250 mg/dL interrupted by a gap is an event only if it had already covered 120 minutes before the gap.
report.research.method.6: Counting: each event is counted once, in the period and on the day in which it starts, also when it continues past midnight. The appendix shows the number of events, their total duration and the longest event for the report period.
report.research.method_note: (GlucoCraft rules where the source does not specify):
report.research.no_standard: The clinical-care consensus describes high glucose by the time above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) and sets targets for those times (Battelino et al., 2019); the ADA Standards of Care do the same ({ada_a}, Table 6.2). Neither defines high-glucose events or a target for their number. The 2023 definition exists only for research, so the count has no published target and no clinical interpretation.

report.statement: GlucoCraft sets no targets or ranges and makes no assessments. Every target and range shown is either taken from the cited published sources (consensus statements, studies and manufacturer documentation), each named as what it is — consensus: ranges and targets (Battelino et al., 2019), tight range (Battelino et al., 2023), CV (Battelino et al., 2019; the study by Monnier et al., 2017); studies: GMI (Bergenstal et al., 2018), GRI (Klonoff et al., 2023) — or set by the user in GlucoCraft's settings. Where GlucoCraft applies a rule of its own (for example the length of a data gap, or the zone of a GRI value), it is labeled as a GlucoCraft rule. GlucoCraft is designed to calculate and display; it sends notifications, prints reports and saves PDF and CSV files only as chosen in its settings or requested by the user. Where colors or the words met / not met appear, they are arithmetic comparisons with the cited target or the custom goal, not clinical assessments.

report.weekly.caption: Time in range, coefficient of variation and mean glucose of each week, on the consensus ranges (Battelino et al., 2019), without targets.
report.weekly.notes.one: The {count} week of 7 days ending on the report's last day, oldest first: time in range, coefficient of variation and mean glucose of each week, calculated on the consensus ranges. The 90-day and the 6-month report show the same weeks. A week with less than 70% sensor active (data received) shows its sensor active and no values, as described in About This Report (Enough data). Weekly values are shown without targets: the consensus targets apply to 14-day periods (Battelino et al., 2019). Differences between weeks are numerical and carry no clinical interpretation.
